- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- If sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.7) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; cap forecast peak at 2–3% above immediate prior high.
- Model underestimates long-term trend (30d) when sentiment is neutral or mixed; add 1–2% to forecast for days 15–30 if sentiment average < 0.3.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misjudges direction; align forecast slope with sentiment momentum (e.g., if sentiment shifts from +0.6 to -0.6, forecast should reverse direction).
- Model tends to lag by 1–3 days in price direction; adjust forecast to match true outcome 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending.
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals unless sentiment confirms strong reversal (e.g., sentiment drops below -0.7 for 3+ days).
